To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the performance of stereo-based pedestrian detection can be improved by using color, disparity, infrared, and multimodal features; (ii) multimodal features can be combined to achieve better detection performance than using unimodal features; and (iii) a single color and infrared camera can be used to achieve multimodal detection.

(1) the combination of color, disparity, infrared features, and stereo geometry significantly outperforms any single feature or stereo geometry in pedestrian detection; (2) the cross-spectral stereo approach, while promising, is not a viable approach to multimodal pedestrian detection; and (3) the combination of multiple modalities is a promising approach to achieving higher detection accuracy and robustness.
the combination of color, infrared, and stereo features is the most effective way to detect pedestrians.
